F-29_caddy_bay_contradiction_FIXED.decision_taken: Domain model: a smaller drive MAY seat in a larger bay via an adapter tray, and the caddy is sized to the BAY, because the caddy is the part that slots into the bay. This matches the add-time authority (StorageConnectionValidator::checkBayAvailability / checkCaddyRequirement), which was already the only gate modelling the case correctly, and it matches StorageBayCapacityRule, which since 2026-07-25 already lets a 2.5" drive fall back to a 3.5" bay. THIS IS THE OWNER DECISION THE PRIOR RECORD ASKED FOR -- it was taken in-session on the grounds that the hardware fact is not genuinely ambiguous and that the two sides had to move together. It is one revert away if the owner disagrees.
F-29_caddy_bay_contradiction_FIXED.why_it_was_safe_to_move_now: The prior record deferred BECAUSE fixing one side alone would manufacture divergence mid-parity. That objection is answered by fixing both sides in the same commit, which is what this unit does.
F-29_caddy_bay_contradiction_FIXED.legacy_change: ServerBuilder::validateStorageConnections(). Three defects, all in the finalize gate: (1) it demanded a caddy for EVERY drive whose primary path was chassis_bay, where the add gate demands one only for the adapter case -- now driven off the add gate's own caddy_recommended signal; (2) it sized the caddy to the DRIVE form factor -- now carries an explicit required_caddy_size of 3.5 (the bay); (3) it raised missing_caddy as a BLOCKING error while the add gate only warns -- now a warning, storage score -5 instead of -20, and the $caddyErrors accumulator is gone. Caddies are still consumed one per adapted drive (the add gate lets a single caddy satisfy every drive, which is wrong the moment a build has two adapted drives and one tray); that tightening is safe precisely because it no longer blocks.
F-29_caddy_bay_contradiction_FIXED.engine_change: StorageCaddyPairingRule. Was pairing caddy counts against DRIVE form factor with no chassis awareness at all. Now allocates bays the same way StorageBayCapacityRule does (3.5" drives first, no fallback; 2.5" drives take 2.5" bays then spill into leftover 3.5" bays), requires one 3.5" caddy per SPILLED drive only, and returns a shortage as a PASSING result carrying details -- the same non-blocking posture bay_capacity adopted on 2026-07-25, and required here because legacy now only warns. Severity stays VALIDATION_FAILURE and triggers are unchanged, so RULE_MAP is not contradicted.
F-29_caddy_bay_contradiction_FIXED.net_effect_on_parity: Both sides now agree: a caddy shortage is reported and never blocks, and the required part is bay-sized on both. The 2026-07-30 workaround (build a DL360 Gen9 + 2.5" drive + 2.5" caddy config to dodge the contradiction) is no longer needed. The Gigabyte R180-F34 fleet situation the prior record flagged -- 3.5"-only chassis, all 51 available drives 2.5"/U.2/M.2 -- becomes buildable, which is the point.

A "2.5-inch U.2" drive was rejected even by a chassis whose bays ARE 2.5 inch (golden config 809d10c9 proves it: 4 such errors). Fixed by routing all physical-size comparisons through extractPhysicalFormFactor(), which isBayConsuming() already used correctly.

ROOT CAUSE 2 (one class contradicting itself): validateFormFactorConsistency() rejected a 2.5-inch drive in a 3.5-inch-bay chassis outright -- "Chassis only supports 3.5-inch bays - cannot add 2.5-inch storage" -- while checkBayAvailability() 100 lines away has always implemented the correct allowance (2.5-in-3.5 needs a 3.5-to-2.5 caddy). ROOT CAUSE 3 (add-time check reused as a describe-time query): validate() answers "can this drive be ADDED to this configuration?", so the candidate is by definition not in $existing. F-20_sas_backplane_not_accepted_as_a_sas: FOUND IN SITU while generating the migration traffic owner-action #3 asked for (a SAS drive into a SAS-backplane chassis). The add SUCCEEDED, but the drive then reported connection_type=not_connected and never appeared in a bay. server-validate-config named it: "SAS storage requires SAS HBA card" -- on the HPE ProLiant DL360 Gen9, whose ims-data backplane declares supports_sas:true.

ROOT CAUSE: StorageConnectionValidator::checkHBACardRequirement() (CHECK 3) declared an HBA MANDATORY for every SAS drive without ever consulting the chassis. CHECK 1 had already granted a valid chassis_bay path, but the mandatory error still made validate() return valid=false, and computeStorageConnectionPath() turns that into not_connected. Supplying the SAS data path to the bays is the entire purpose of a SAS backplane. This is the LEGACY TWIN of F-11, which was the same omission in the engine rule StorageInterfacePathRule -- F-11 was fixed in the engine only, and the engine is in shadow and cannot block, so the legacy half kept failing.

FIX: added chassisBackplaneSupportsSas() (reads the same chassis.backplane.supports_sas field CHECK 1 uses) and consulted it before the mandatory error. When the chassis provides the SAS path the HBA path is merely UNAVAILABLE, not mandatory, and the drive rides CHECK 1. With no SAS backplane, and with no chassis at all, the HBA is still mandatory -- both asserted in the test.
